title: Consistency
measures: Whether the student's work is spread through the sprint rather than squeezed into a few days: share of days with real work and how early the work started.
inputs: commit dates (author's own date) with clean line statistics
computation: Ridge model on two features: active-days share (C_AWR) and day of the first commit (C_first_active_day). A student with no activity scores 0. Late-work share, longest idle run and burstiness are computed and reported as features but add nothing measurable in the validation data.
output_scale: 0 = no activity or only at the very end, 1 = steady work from the first days.
gates: Needs at least 5 days of the sprint for a provisional score; before that: not available (a rhythm cannot be read earlier).
validation: 144 real student-sprints, student-disjoint 5-fold CV against assistant-written rubric ratings: MAE 0.058 (active-days baseline 0.078), Pearson 0.92. The proposal's four features alone do not beat active days.
limits: Assumes a 14-day sprint in the validation data.
Commit dates are the author's local date; commits made on one day under another time zone can shift a day.
A student whose work is in someone else's commits (pair programming under one account) looks inconsistent.

warnings.provisional: Computed on the part of the sprint that has passed.
warnings.feature .* missing: A feature was missing and the training median was used.

typical_problems.likely_cause: all commits on the last days, or commits pushed in bulk from a local history

typical_problems.symptom: zero consistency for a student who worked
typical_problems.likely_cause: author e-mail not mapped to the student
